title: The Listening Bell
premise: When a construction crew breaks into an unmapped tunnel beneath the drowned town of Hollowmere, urban explorer Freya Underhill is the only one who recognizes the bell-shaped chamber at its heart — because they've been hearing it ring in their dreams for twelve years, ever since they survived a collapse that killed their friends. The door was sealed from the inside by the town's founders, who bound something in the well below and fed it with ritual consent: every generation, the town chose someone to 'listen' so the rest could live safe. Now the seal is broken, the crew is being taken one by one, and Freya must finish the founders' ritual — but the ritual requires a willing listener, and the thing in the well has learned to speak in the voices of everyone Freya has lost. In the end, Freya rings the bell themselves, choosing to stay as the new listener rather than let the crew's survivor carry the burden, sealing the door from the inside at last.
about_author: Coral Ravensworth is the pen name of a former municipal archivist who spent a decade cataloguing sealed records of flooded settlements across the north of England. Their fiction blends documentary precision with folk horror, and they claim every novel begins with a real document they can no longer find.

chapters.title: The Survey That Isn't
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Twelve years after surviving the Hollowmere collapse, Freya returns when news breaks that an excavation crew has found tunnels absent from every survey. They tell themselves it's closure, not compulsion. The beat is dread disguised as curiosity — Freya lies to themselves even as their hands shake on the train platform.

chapters.title: Sealed From Within
chapters.summary: Alternating Freya and site foreman Denny Okafor's POVs. The crew shows Freya the iron door: bolted shut from the tunnel side, hinges fused, yet warm to the touch. Freya recognizes the bell motif carved into it from dreams they've never described aloud. The beat is the horror of being known by something you've never met.

chapters.title: What the Founders Kept
chapters.summary: Freya's POV, interwoven with archival fragments. Researching in the county records office, Freya finds Hollowmere's founding covenant: a well, a bell, and a 'Listener' chosen each generation so the town could prosper. The last entry is dated the year of the collapse — the year Freya went down. The beat is guilt curdling into suspicion.

chapters.title: The First Ringing
chapters.summary: Denny's POV. Overnight, the youngest crew member hears the bell toll underground; by morning he's gone, his lamp found still burning beside the door, which now stands ajar. Freya arrives to find the crew refusing to leave — contracts, debts, a foreman who won't report it. The beat is complicity: everyone choosing survival over truth.

chapters.title: Voices in the Water
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Descending past the door, Freya finds the bell chamber above a black well and hears their dead friends' voices rising with the water level — including apologies only the real Tomás would know. The thing is learning them. The beat is grief weaponized, and Freya's first admission that the noises were never explainable.

chapters.title: The Covenant of Consent
chapters.summary: Crew member Priya's POV. Priya discovers the ritual's terms in a founder's ledger: the binding holds only if the Listener consents freely; coercion voids it and the well refills. The crew realizes someone must volunteer — or be made to want to. The beat is moral corrosion as the survivors begin quietly weighing each other.

chapters.title: A Vote Underground
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV through Denny. Trapped by a partial collapse that seals the entrance, the crew holds a terrible, deniable 'vote' on who listens. Freya refuses to let it happen, revealing they've heard the bell for twelve years — the thing has been calling them since the first collapse. The beat is betrayal and the corruption of desperate power.

chapters.title: The Well Refills
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The water rises fast now; the entity stops pretending, wearing all the voices at once and offering each survivor exactly what they need to say yes. Denny tries to force Priya toward the bell and dies in the flood surge — taken, not drowned. The beat is terror stripped of ambiguity: the price of survival comes due.

chapters.title: The Listening Bell
chapters.summary: Freya's POV, climax. With the chamber flooding, Freya understands the ritual's final clause: the Listener must ring the bell themselves, willingly, and remain. They lie to the entity using Tomás's voice against it, climb the bell tower scaffold, and pull the rope as the water takes their feet. The beat is sacrifice as authorship — justice outside any law.

chapters.title: Sealed From Within, Again
chapters.summary: Priya's POV, epilogue. Priya surfaces alone, tells officials a collapse took the others, and watches the shaft be poured with concrete. At night she hears one soft toll and answers it aloud — 'I remember you' — keeping the listening alive from outside. The beat is haunted survival: the price paid, and the debt inherited.
